text: I have studied the Signs carved on seals and monument walls for over twenty years.
I cannot read them. No one can. I say this plainly, even though it disappoints people.
I catalog every Sign sequence I encounter, hoping patterns will emerge across enough examples.
Certain Signs appear almost always at the end of a sequence, which may mark something like a title or a place.
I do not claim to know what that mark means. I only note that it repeats.
Kalen and I disagree about meaning, but his wall-phase dating tells me which Sign-styles are older.
The Signs on the oldest Citadel brick differ subtly from the Signs on the newer, post-Turning brick.
This may mean the script changed slightly after the Turning, or that different carvers simply had different habits.
I cannot yet tell which explanation is correct, and it troubles me more than I let on.
Elira's old tally-records used a simplified numeric version of some Signs for counting goods.
That numeric use may be the closest thing to a confirmed meaning for any Sign I've found.
Doran once asked whether old boundary stones' Signs matched current terrace markers. They didn't, quite.
Fen brought me a fragment from the Old Canal Bed with a Sign sequence I hadn't cataloged before.
It may be from an older phase of the settlement than anything else I've recorded.
Sena's oral-history timeline and Kalen's stonework and my Sign-style shift all point toward the same period of change.
I don't think that convergence is coincidence, even though none of us can fully explain it alone.
